entries.title: A long caller or importer list arrives capped and says so
entries.summary: check_references lists at most 50 importing files per name and get_call_hierarchy at most 100 callers and 100 callees, nearest first. Each reply keeps the whole counts and says when it cut (import_references_total and import_references_truncated; callers_truncated and callees_truncated), so a cut list never reads as complete. On this repository a check_references reply for Path went from 99,795 bytes to 29,745 as served, and get_call_hierarchy for resolve_repo at depth 2 from 478,337 to 31,938, which had been over the response limit as JSON. max_import_results and max_results set the cap; 0 lists everything.

entries.title: A dead-code answer over withheld files reads them instead of refusing
entries.summary: When the index withheld a file for size, find_dead_code capped every finding below its default threshold and told the session to raise a setting no tool can change. When withheld files are the only reason, it now reads their imports from disk with the indexer's own extractor and resolver, so a withheld importer counts like an indexed one, and the answer is published at full confidence with the files it read named. A file that cannot stand in for an indexed one (unreadable, not text, a data or config file, or a language whose edges the index adds at load) keeps the cap, and check_delete_safe still refuses a delete over withheld files (L-352).

entries.title: A change under an ignored path no longer runs a watcher pass
entries.summary: The watcher counted every added, modified or deleted event before it looked at any ignore rule, so a gitignored folder rewritten all day ran an index pass per batch, and a new-folder event made that pass a walk of the whole tree. Added and modified events are now checked against the rules every walk of the folder applies, read again per batch. A batch of only ignored events runs no pass, and deletions and .gitignore edits always pass (#1581).

entries.title: A watch event outside the watched folder no longer fails the whole batch
entries.summary: The watcher keyed every event by its path relative to the watched folder, and an event path not under that spelling raised and failed the whole batch: the other edits in it stayed unindexed and a retry was scheduled. A folder reached through a symlink made every batch fail this way. An event whose real path lies under the folder's real path is now indexed under the folder; any other path is dropped with a warning, and the rest of the batch is indexed (#1582). A key-anchored secret after a closing subscript or JSON-escaped quotes is now redacted (#1576).

entries.title: One locked file no longer fails the whole re-index
entries.summary: An incremental re-index read each edited file to hash it, and when that read failed, as a sharing violation does on Windows while an editor or antivirus holds a file, the whole call failed and every other edit in the walk stayed unindexed while the lock held. A file change detection cannot read now reads as changed: it keeps its stored rows, is named in unread_files and keeps coverage incomplete, and the rest of the walk is saved (L-350).

entries.title: A failed watcher update is retried without another file edit
entries.summary: When the watcher's save failed, including while it waited for another writer's lock, it recorded the failure and waited for new events, so edits it had already been told about could stay unindexed indefinitely. A failed update now keeps the folder pending and retries a full walk with a capped backoff, naming the files of the failed batches, and get_watch_status reports the pending work. A file that stays locked with no edit pending keeps its coverage record without holding the watcher in a retry. Reported and fixed by @MariusAdrian88 (#1567).

entries.title: The index cache sees another process's write and stops reloading for nothing
entries.summary: A write that another process committed while this one loaded the index was cached as if it were already included, so the older index was served until some other write moved the stamp; the cache is now keyed at the stamp taken before the read. An incremental re-index patches the index in memory again instead of rebuilding it from every stored row after its own coverage write. A repository with Racket files no longer loads the whole index on every run to read the reader version. A search no longer hashes statistics and counts files for a write-back the store would refuse: it asks first.

entries.title: A delete blocked only by a file import says so
entries.summary: check_delete_safe counted every file that imports a symbol's file as an external use of that symbol, so a function its module never exports came back external_uses_blocking with "1 other file(s) in this repo import this" when no file used it. When the reference search reads the importing files and the symbol's own file and finds the name in none of them, the verdict is now file_import_only: still a block, with the reading that would settle it named. A use in the symbol's own file, a search that failed, or a file the search could not read keeps external_uses_blocking.

entries.title: A subfolder index reads the root .gitignore, and watch-install needs no elevated shell
entries.summary: Indexing a subfolder read only the .gitignore files from that folder down, so it added files the repository root's .gitignore excludes, and the next full index removed them with no message. The subfolder walk, paths= from a subfolder and index_file now read the .gitignore chain from the git root down. On Windows, watch-install registered a logon task with no user, which Windows refuses from a shell that is not elevated; the task now names the calling user. Both reported by @rknighton (#1563, #1564).

entries.title: An index on an unplugged drive survives server start
entries.summary: Every server start deleted the index of a folder that was not there at that moment, so a folder on an unplugged USB drive or an unmounted volume lost its index and needed a full re-index when the drive came back. The sweep now deletes only when the drive that holds the folder is present, keeps the index when it cannot tell, and no longer checks network folders on Windows at start.

entries.title: A Bearer token with ~ + / = or ! is redacted whole
entries.summary: The redactor cut a Bearer token at the first character outside letters, digits, _, - and ., so part of a token, or all of a Salesforce token, could reach a tool answer. It now takes every character RFC 6750 allows, plus ! with or without backslash escapes, and runtime trace redaction uses the same pattern. Reported by @goranai, who also sent a fix in #1559.

entries.title: get_changed_symbols says that its cross_repo argument does nothing
entries.summary: get_changed_symbols accepted a cross_repo argument that nothing read, so a Python caller who set it got a local-only blast radius with no sign the flag did nothing. A call that passes it now emits a FutureWarning saying it has no effect and is deprecated. The argument is still accepted, so no existing call breaks under default warning filters. MCP callers are unaffected.

entries.title: Every license covers all three tools, and a $9.99 Freelance license
entries.summary: Licenses are now one price per tier for jCodeMunch, jDocMunch and jDataMunch together: Builder $99, Studio $449, Platform $2,499, one-time. A new Freelance license, $9.99 one-time, covers one person's own freelance work and side projects that brought in under $10,000 in the last 12 months. Licenses bought before today stay valid. LICENSE is now version 1.3, and the init closing line, the license reminder and the README carry the new prices.

entries.title: A capped re-index names the files kept from an earlier index, and compact blast radius keeps every top-level key
entries.summary: When an agent re-index runs under a smaller max_folder_files than the index it replaces, the warning, resolve_repo and init now say how many indexed files were kept from the earlier index instead of printing an indexed count above the cap with no explanation. The compact form of get_blast_radius now keeps cross_repo_confirmed_count and the include_decisions git history, which it used to drop without a word.

entries.title: A folder inside a Git worktree is matched to the indexed checkout
entries.summary: resolve_repo on a folder inside a linked worktree of an indexed checkout now names that checkout as the index to read from, as it already did for the worktree root. It walks up to the nearest .git the way git does, with no subprocess, and an independent repository nested inside still answers for itself.

entries.title: A Ruby import never resolves to another language's file
entries.summary: An extensionless require or require_relative in a .rb or .rake file now resolves only to a .rb file. It no longer becomes an import edge to a Python, JavaScript, Go or SQL file Ruby cannot load, so find_dead_code, find_importers and get_blast_radius stop treating such a file as imported in a mixed repository.

entries.title: A Go file no go.mod covers is never proven dead; a C or C++ caller list says it is a text match
entries.summary: find_dead_code no longer reports a Go file as provably dead, and check_delete_safe no longer calls it safe to delete, when no go.mod the index read maps its imports. get_call_hierarchy finds C and C++ callers in four more layouts: the same file, behind an umbrella header, a definition that skips its header, and a caller that writes its own prototype. A C or C++ answer now says its callers came from a text match and may be incomplete.

entries.title: A compact answer says when a secret was redacted; the mcp floor admits no advised SDK
entries.summary: A compact answer kept the notes the server adds last only when it was sent as JSON: that a secret was redacted, that the session is near its token budget, and which symbols were already sent. Every compact answer keeps them now. The mcp dependency floor is 1.30.0, the first release with no published advisory.

entries.title: get_ranked_context says when no symbol has the name you asked for
entries.summary: Asked for a name no symbol has, get_ranked_context returned rows that only share words with it and said nothing about it on a default install. It now says no symbol has that name, as search_symbols does, and its verdict reads low confidence.

entries.title: a cut-short text search is never read as a complete one
entries.summary: The deletion check could call a function unused when another file used it, because it read only the first page of a text search. It now reads the whole match set and treats a search that skipped files as unsettled. The Grep shortcut no longer answers a search that could miss a file the index left out for size.

entries.title: a lock file is never on disk without the metadata that names its holder
entries.summary: The locks that keep two processes from saving one index at once, and that bound index-file runs, could be taken by two processes at the same moment: the lock file was briefly empty while its holder wrote it, and a rival deleted it as corrupt. The holder's details are now linked into place whole.

entries.title: get_symbol_source sends a docstring once, and announce_model is listed only when it can act
entries.summary: get_symbol_source no longer repeats a docstring that is already inside the source it returns: 9.97% fewer characters per reply on this repository's own index. announce_model is listed only while adaptive_tiering is on; it stays callable.

entries.title: compact schemas are on by default, and a hidden parameter keeps its type
entries.summary: compact_schemas defaults to true: the core tool definitions drop from 6,208 to 3,992 tokens. Set it false for the full schemas. A hidden parameter sent as a string is still converted to its type.

entries.title: the server's instructions name a tool only while the session is served it
entries.summary: The instructions a client keeps when it defers tool schemas name only tools the session is served, and tell a session that serves get_call_hierarchy that it answers who calls a function.

entries.title: get_call_hierarchy with no depth returns the direct callers and callees
entries.summary: get_call_hierarchy called without depth walks one hop, the direct callers and callees, instead of three; pass depth (2 to 5) to walk further.

entries.title: an annotation that spells the target's name no longer makes a same-named declaration count as a use
entries.summary: check_delete_safe and check_edit_safe find a same-named declaration's name line by its exact spelling within its signature, so an annotation such as @FileAnno above it no longer counts the declaration as a use of the target.

entries.title: a delete preflight counts a call on a one-line method that shares the target's name
entries.summary: check_delete_safe and check_edit_safe no longer hide a call on the one line of a same-named method, field or property; a declaration line counts when it calls the name beyond the declarations on it.

entries.title: a repeated find_references or get_blast_radius answers from the index another process just wrote
entries.summary: A repeated find_references or get_blast_radius call no longer answers from a cached result after the file watcher, the index-file hook, refresh or a second server rewrote the index; the cached answer is tied to the load of the index it came from.

entries.title: a search row caps its signature at 200 characters and says when it was cut
entries.summary: search_symbols now sends at most 200 characters of a long signature in its default reply and marks a cut row signature_truncated: true; get_symbol_source still returns the whole signature. On a repository with very long multi-line signatures, a search reply is much smaller.

entries.title: a delete preflight no longer hides a caller inside a same-named method
entries.summary: check_delete_safe and check_edit_safe now count a call inside another method that shares the target's name, so a used method is no longer graded safe to delete. Their blockers also name the line of the first use instead of line 0.

entries.title: a comment after a base list no longer hides the base
entries.summary: Class hierarchy, implementation and call-graph answers now find a class's base when a comment follows the extends or implements list, or sits inside a multi-line Python base list. Before, such a class had no base and dropped out of its parent's subtree.

entries.title: a compact answer says when a row's code changed since the index read it
entries.summary: A compact search or symbol answer now says when the file a row points at was edited after indexing, where before it reached the agent byte for byte the same as an answer about current code. Answers where every row is current keep exactly the bytes they had.

entries.title: a forced re-index keeps the AI summaries a provider could not replace
entries.summary: When the configured summarizer cannot run, a forced or edit-time re-index keeps the AI summaries already stored instead of writing signature fallbacks over them, and the result names the provider that could not run.

entries.title: two HTTP sessions that send the same token keep their own tool tier
entries.summary: On the streamable-http transport, each session keeps its own tool tier even when every client sends the same bearer token, and a session's tier is dropped when the session ends.

entries.title: a review capsule names the symbol a renamed function was
entries.summary: assemble_task_context keeps the previous symbol id on a renamed row of its changed-symbols stage, so a review capsule says which symbol a rename came from, not only its old name.

entries.title: a watch-service probe that could not ask reads as unknown, and a renamed function reads as renamed
entries.summary: get_watch_status reports unknown, with the reason, when the service manager could not be asked, instead of reporting the watcher stopped. get_changed_symbols reports a renamed function as one renamed row with its previous name and symbol id, instead of an added row and a removed row.

entries.title: a Go program is an entry point, a review capsule says what changed, and a forced summary refresh keeps stored summaries
entries.summary: The dead-code tools treat a Go package main program as an entry point. A review-mode assemble_task_context names the symbols that changed. A forced summarize_repo whose configured provider cannot start keeps stored AI summaries and names the provider.

entries.title: the agent selector's top OpenAI model is no longer one OpenAI retires on 2026-12-11
entries.summary: With agent_selector on, the top OpenAI default is gpt-6.1-sol, the model OpenAI names to replace o3 when o3 shuts down on 2026-12-11.

entries.title: Go imports between packages of one module resolve through go.mod
entries.summary: A Go import by module path now reaches the package it names, so most packages of one module no longer read as dead or unimported.

entries.title: a savings count is kept when servers stop together
entries.summary: A server that stops while another holds the savings file keeps its counts in a pending file, and the next write adds them in.

entries.title: a compact answer gives back a list or dict inside a table row
entries.summary: The generic compact encoder sends a table cell holding a list or dict as JSON, so it decodes back to the list or dict instead of a string.

entries.title: a tool count is kept when servers stop together
entries.summary: A server that stops while another holds the tool-count file keeps its counts in a pending file, and the next write adds them in.

entries.title: check_references sends the same answer in up to 46% fewer characters
entries.summary: check_references sends the same answer in up to 46% fewer characters: a compact encoding, with the decoded answer unchanged.

entries.title: a C function shows the callers that reach it through its header
entries.summary: A C or C++ function shows the callers that reach it through the header that declares it, in get_call_hierarchy, get_impact_preview and get_blast_radius.

entries.title: a Cursor read count whose lock wait runs out is kept, not dropped
entries.summary: A Cursor read count whose lock wait runs out goes to a pending file and is folded in by the next count, instead of being dropped. This fixes the known issue named in 1.108.453.

entries.title: Cursor's agent reads of indexed code are counted beside its jCodeMunch lookups
entries.summary: With `init --cursor-hooks`, Cursor's agent reads of indexed code are counted beside its jCodeMunch lookups, as a floor of what the hooks saw. Known issue: a count whose lock wait times out is dropped without notice; the next release fixes it.

entries.title: the tool counters say how many calls found nothing
entries.summary: The tool counters record how many calls found nothing.

entries.title: a full index no longer pays for work nobody has asked for yet
entries.summary: A full index no longer computes search statistics or counts every file's tokens while it saves. The first search computes the statistics and stores them for the next process, and a file's token count is taken the first time a response credits that file.

entries.title: a trusted folder is matched by the folder it names
entries.summary: A trusted_folders entry set through JCODEMUNCH_TRUSTED_FOLDERS is resolved before it is compared, so an entry that reaches the folder through a symlink or a .. segment (every macOS temp folder is under the /var link) matches it, in whitelist and blacklist mode. A relative entry, or one whose ~name names no user, still matches nothing and is logged.

entries.title: an index that is missing something says so
entries.summary: A search over an index that left files out for size says how many. An agent working in a second copy of an indexed repo is told why the index is silent there and how to index it. The runtime identity resource and install-status carry a build digest, so two installs of one version can be told apart.

entries.title: an edit no longer starts an unbounded pile of index runs
entries.summary: The edit hook runs at most one index-file per checkout and two on the machine; queued paths are indexed by the live run. A filtered search_symbols names its filter instead of claiming the whole index lacks the symbol. get_file_outline accepts file= without calling it ignored. A file whose cached copy is missing says so, and re-indexing that one file repairs it.

entries.title: on macOS, a process is identified by its creation time
entries.summary: On macOS the lock files and the process registry could not tell a process from a later one that got the same PID, so a dead watcher's lock could read as held. The start time now comes from libproc, and the munch://runtime/identity resource reads the same source.

entries.title: a running server that serves older code than is installed is named
entries.summary: Upgrading the package does not reach a server that is already running. install-status now lists the running servers on this index store and marks each one restart required, current or unknown; it reports only and stops nothing. USER_GUIDE.md gains "Upgrading a running server", with the three ways to read the serving version and a deploy check.

entries.title: a write that changes no symbol leaves other processes' indexes in place
entries.summary: Every process holding an index reloaded all of it whenever the .db changed, including writes that touch no symbol: embeddings, runtime ingests, SCIP, BM25 statistics. Symbol and file writes now stamp a content generation, and a process keeps its copy when the meta table is exactly as it loaded it. With eight readers and one runtime write a second, reader p99 fell from 1284.9 ms to 138.8 ms.

entries.title: a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint is sent a model it serves
entries.summary: With OPENAI_API_BASE pointing at a local server and no model named, the summarizer sent OpenAI's hosted default, which a local server does not serve, while config --check showed qwen3-coder. One rule now picks the default from the base URL, read by both: api.openai.com gets gpt-6-luna, any other base gets qwen3-coder. A model you name is used as before.

entries.title: a built-in default names a model the provider still serves
entries.summary: The agent selector's Anthropic and Google orders and the Gemini summarizer default named models a new install could not call, and the OpenAI defaults named models OpenAI removes on 2027-01-14. Every default now names a current model, read on the provider's own pages, and a scan keeps the retired ids out. A model you set in config is used as before. A license_key in a project .jcodemunch.jsonc now logs a warning instead of being dropped in silence.

entries.title: a Java or Kotlin class used only by its own package is not reported dead
entries.summary: Classes in one Java or Kotlin package use each other with no import line, and find_dead_code reads only the import graph, so a class used only by its own package was reported dead at confidence 1.0. A file's own package is now an implicit wildcard import: one edge per class name the file uses, kept only where the package declares the name. Same-package use now shows in find_references, and in dependency cycles and coupling. The first index after upgrading re-parses every file.

entries.title: a framework profile's ignore patterns hold on every route that walks into an index
entries.summary: 1.108.440 ranked a framework profile's ignore patterns below a project's own on the full walk and in index_file. Three other routes never read the profile: the watcher's fast path, refresh's discovery, and a directory named in index_folder(paths=[...]). Each could put an express project's coverage/ report back into an index the full walk had kept it out of. All of them now use the profile the full walk uses, ranked below the project's and the call's own patterns, so a !pattern negation still wins. A file named in paths= is still indexed on request.

entries.title: a project's own ignore negation wins over a framework profile's default
entries.summary: A framework profile ignore pattern (the express coverage/ default, for one) used to come after the project .jcodemunch.jsonc list, and ignore matching is last-match-wins, so a project negation such as !tools/coverage/** lost and the directory dropped out of the index. Profile patterns now have the lowest precedence, below the global and project config and any per-call list. index_file follows the same order, and its refusal names the negation as the way to override a profile pattern. Reported by @dkiaulakis (#1398).

entries.title: tokens_saved is a token count, not bytes divided by 4
entries.summary: tokens_saved used to divide saved bytes by 4, which undercounted on Claude. Each indexed file is now counted once with tiktoken cl100k_base when its index is saved, scaled to Claude by a ratio measured per language (savings_tokenizer: openai uses the raw count). tiktoken fetches its encoding file once, on first use, in the background; tokenizer_download: false turns that off, and the per-language table is the fallback. _meta.tokens_saved_basis names the path. Totals already recorded are not rescaled.

entries.title: an index that holds a small part of the tree reads incomplete, not fresh
entries.summary: get_watch_status compared only the indexed revision with HEAD, so an index built at HEAD that held a sliver of the tree read fresh. Each repo now also reports index_completeness (complete, incomplete or unknown) with the indexed and tracked file counts, any_incomplete says when any repo is incomplete, and any_completeness_unknown says when a repo could not be counted, which is never reported as complete.

entries.title: a file the index withheld is not answered as a missing file
entries.summary: A file over max_file_size used to get the same answer as a path that does not exist, so an agent told the file was absent went looking for an older copy. get_file_outline and get_file_content now say the file is withheld, give its size and the limit, and how to index it, and the verdict says absence is not proven. A Bearer token inside a quoted Authorization header is now redacted too.

entries.title: a call that names paths= never replaces the rest of the index
entries.summary: index_folder with paths= and incremental=False used to save the listed files as the whole index and drop every other file while reporting success. A call that names paths= now keeps every stored file it did not list, on every route, and says how many it kept.

entries.title: a Kotlin import of a top-level declaration reaches the file that declares it
entries.summary: An import of a top-level Kotlin function, val, object or typealias, or of a second class in a file named after another one, now counts as an import of the file that declares it, so find_importers and the dead-code tools no longer read that file as unused. Java's route to a Kotlin file's top-level functions (the FileKt class) resolves the same way.

entries.title: the full tool surface no longer loads six schemas into every request
entries.summary: On the full tool surface, the six core tools no longer load up front in clients that defer MCP tools, so they stop riding in every request. This reverses the full-surface half of 1.108.389's up-front load: an agent there now makes one ToolSearch call before its first core-tool call. The default counter surface is unchanged.

entries.title: the bundled local encoder no longer pays for padding
entries.summary: The bundled local encoder trims each batch to its longest real text instead of running every text at 256 positions, several times faster on symbol-sized texts with identical vectors. An empty batch no longer loads the model, and JCODEMUNCH_LOCAL_EMBED_THREADS sets its CPU threads.

entries.title: a Java or Kotlin wildcard import is an edge to each class the file uses
entries.summary: A Java or Kotlin file that writes import a.b.*; now counts as importing each class it uses from that package, so find_importers and check_delete_safe no longer read those classes as unused. Re-index a JVM repository once to pick it up.

entries.title: a read re-indexes the files that changed since the index was built
entries.summary: Before a read tool answers on a git repository, the server asks git which files changed since the index was built and re-indexes them, so a rebase, a branch switch or an outside edit no longer leaves a search serving old code. get_call_hierarchy now says on which lines each caller calls the target, so finding a call site takes no extra reads.

entries.title: a Java or Kotlin import is an edge to the file that declares it
entries.summary: A Java or Kotlin import now resolves to the .java or .kt file that declares the class, so a JVM repository's import graph has edges and the importer, dependency, dead-code and delete-safety tools see who uses a file. Re-indexing a folder where nothing changed no longer loads every stored symbol row to compare against.

entries.title: a hook answers in about a second
entries.summary: A hook command now answers in about a second: a bare hook command runs its handler without importing the server, so an answered Grep takes 1.07 to 1.21 s for the whole hook process, where it took 5.1 s before, and the Grep answer reads the source files its freshness check just proved unchanged.

entries.title: the published benchmark counts the answer an agent receives
entries.summary: The published token benchmark is re-measured on the text the server actually sends on a default install: jCodeMunch uses 96.2% fewer tokens per lookup on average than grep-and-read across the 15-lookup benchmark, and every one of the 15 lookups now returns symbols.

entries.title: the Grep answer replies right after a large index is built
entries.summary: Right after a large index is built, the opt-in Grep answer now replies inside its 4-second budget: on freshly indexed Home Assistant copies, first searches that used to run out of time answer in 1.3 s, 0.9 s and 1.0 s. Text search reads its candidate files on a small pool of threads and gives the same answer. The token benchmark now counts the response an agent actually receives.

entries.title: a function assigned to a member is a JavaScript symbol
entries.summary: CommonJS functions are symbols: a function, arrow or generator assigned to a member at module scope (res.send = function ..., exports.f = ..., Foo.prototype.bar = ...) is now indexed, and a bound function's signature is its header, not its whole body. On Windows the Grep answer confirms its cached copies with one directory listing per folder and no longer decodes imports it never reads, and the one search per session that carries the steering hint keeps the compact encoding.

entries.title: the Grep answer reaches large repositories
entries.summary: On a large repository the opt-in Grep answer now replies inside its 4-second budget instead of letting the Grep run unanswered: on a 23,186-file Home Assistant index, a Grep over homeassistant/ is answered in 2.0 s with a warm file cache (it needed 6.2 s). upgrade and init --hooks now print the tool-surface offer that install-status shows, and receipt and diagnose read the savings file the same way the savings meter does, so a malformed file no longer crashes receipt.

entries.title: a project config file can only tighten settings
entries.summary: A project's .jcodemunch.jsonc can tighten the settings that decide which folders are trusted, what is read or run, what is sent off the machine and what a summarizer may bill, but never loosen them past your own config. Each key it cannot apply as written is logged once by name.

entries.title: a file that fails to parse no longer lets a search claim a name is absent
entries.summary: A file whose parse fails or runs past its time budget now counts as withheld, so a search refuses to call a name absent instead of answering absent on an index that skipped the file. A fresh server process also reuses the search statistics stored in the index instead of rebuilding them before its first search.

entries.title: the shared parse cache never serves what an older parser emitted
entries.summary: On a host that sets JCODEMUNCH_PARSE_CACHE, the re-index a parser upgrade forces now parses every file again instead of reading the old symbols back from the cache.

entries.title: a starter pack installs in a few megabytes, and a file tree costs a third of the characters
entries.summary: install-pack writes a pack to disk as it downloads instead of holding it in memory, and get_file_tree sends the same tree in a third to a half of the characters.

entries.title: re-indexing one file by path keeps a partial index marked partial
entries.summary: Saving one edited file by path no longer marks an index the file cap cut short as complete, so searches over it keep saying it is partial.

entries.title: the file cap limits what one call parses, not what the index keeps
entries.summary: An agent's capped index call no longer shrinks an index the command line built past the cap, and the opt-in Grep answer counts every match of a large Grep.

entries.title: a search on a capped index says, in its answer, that the index is partial
entries.summary: A search on an index the file cap cut short now says so in the answer itself, with the file counts and the setting to raise.

entries.title: a wrong call through order names a call that works
entries.summary: A misspelled or refused call through order now names a call that works, and a turned-off tool says to ask the user.

entries.title: a search credits the tokens it saved on a fresh install's index
entries.summary: Searches on a fresh index now credit the tokens they saved, so an install that only searched reports savings.

entries.title: a search for library code ranks the library above its tutorial and example copies
entries.summary: Searching for library code now returns the library's own symbols ahead of the copies in its examples, tutorials and docs samples, the way test files were already weighted down.

entries.title: a class comes back as its outline, and an import finds the file in its own language
entries.summary: Fetching a class now returns its outline, each method collapsed to its signature; pass class_body="full" for the whole body. An import with no extension now finds the file in the importer's own language first.

entries.title: the license terms read the same in the terminal, the package and the site
entries.summary: The license lines in the terminal and the package's own descriptions now say what the site says: work use at a for-profit company, or for client or paid work, needs a license.

entries.title: graph tools resolve each import once per loaded index, and a savings file holding the wrong type is refused, not frozen
entries.summary: Graph tools (dependency graph, importers, blast radius) now resolve each import once per loaded index instead of on every call, so a second call on a large repo answers in a fraction of the time. A savings file that parses but holds a string or another wrong type where the meter adds a number is now refused with a warning and the counts kept, instead of silently freezing the meter.

entries.title: a C or C++ #include resolves where the compiler finds it, and Go callers in the same package are found
entries.summary: A C or C++ #include now resolves where the compiler finds it: beside the including file, then at the repo root and under include/ and src/, so a C++ repo's import graph is no longer missing most of its header edges. Asking who calls a Go function now finds callers in the same package, which call each other with no import. The next index re-parses every file.

entries.title: a savings meter that stops measuring says so, and Rails views are indexed
entries.summary: A savings meter that stops measuring now says so: receipt, diagnose and get_session_stats report whether the lifetime total is current, stale or unknown, and a write can no longer wipe or lose counts. Ruby ERB templates (.erb) are indexed, so Rails views are searchable. reflect --apply-weights writes the tuning file the server actually reads when CODE_INDEX_PATH is set.

entries.title: a search for a name nothing carries says so on a default install
entries.summary: A search for a name that no symbol carries now says so in the answer itself, even on a default install that hides metadata: the results stay, marked as sharing words with the query only, and the answer is never presented as proof the name is absent. The work-license reminder's buy link now says where it was shown.

entries.title: a rare work-license reminder, never shown to a license holder
entries.summary: Using jCodeMunch for work needs a license, and a machine is now reminded of that rarely: 7 days after its first index, then at most once every 30 days, as one stderr line after a command a person reads or one field on a tool answer. Never with a license key, on CI, or after `jcodemunch-mcp config set license_reminder false`. Nothing is sent.

entries.title: a stdio server exits when the process that started it is gone, and storage reports how much disk the index uses
entries.summary: A stdio server now exits when the client that started it is gone, checked every 5 seconds, even if something else holds its input open. jcodemunch-mcp storage prints the index store's path and total, then each index by name, largest first. A query that names a tool, bare or with the host prefix, finds that tool first.

entries.title: watch-all leaves temp and idle indexes unwatched, and agents sharing an index stop reloading it
entries.summary: watch-all skips indexes under a temp folder and ones idle for 14 days, and watch exits when it cannot watch. Agents sharing one index no longer make each other reload it, and the first search on a large index tokenizes faster. init --git-hook re-indexes the files a branch switch changed. A key holder is never shown where to buy a license.

entries.title: get_class_hierarchy and find_implementations read a base list written after a colon
entries.summary: For a C# class Circle : IShape, get_class_hierarchy names IShape as an ancestor and find_implementations("IShape") returns Circle. The same holds for Kotlin, Swift, C++ and Rust base lists, Ruby's class A < B, and Scala and Dart's extends B with T. An enum's underlying type (enum E : byte) is not read as a base. No re-index is needed.

entries.title: a failed summarizer keeps the summaries it had, and tool descriptions open with the agent's question
entries.summary: summarize_repo(force=true) keeps each stored summary when the provider fails for that symbol, and reports provider_fallbacks and previous_summaries_kept. Seventeen tool descriptions open with the question an agent asks, so a host that searches descriptions finds them. The plugin listing and the MCP registry show the jCodeMunch icon.

entries.title: a file pattern means the same thing in every tool, and the rate_limit config key turns the limit on
entries.summary: A file_pattern with a slash is anchored at the repo root and a bare one matches at any depth, the same way in search_text, the index store and every scope check. The rate_limit key in config.jsonc now turns on the HTTP rate limit, in the documented order. On Windows, init writes Codex's entry as the bare command name when PATH finds the same install. The CLI's license link points at the current site.

entries.title: the server instructions name the tools in the first 512 characters, and tool names hold across 1.x
entries.summary: Clients that read only the first 512 characters of the server instructions, Codex among them, now see the core tool names. Tool names are frozen for 1.x: a renamed tool keeps its old name as an alias for at least 30 days. Writing a file into a watched folder no longer re-walks the whole repo, and an install that never ran init sees the license terms once.

entries.title: a redirected Grep can carry the index's answer, and a substring search opens only the files that can match
entries.summary: With JCODEMUNCH_HOOK_GREP_ANSWER=1, the PreToolUse hook answers a redirected Grep with the search_text result instead of asking for a second turn; it is off by default. Indexing writes a trigram bitmap per cached file, so a substring search_text skips files that cannot match; a cold index takes about 10% longer.

entries.title: a text search returns the code it found, and a retired tool name says what replaced it
entries.summary: When search_text's matches fall inside a few small functions or classes, the page carries each one's source once, so an agent can edit without opening the file. Calling get_symbol or get_symbols, retired in March, now returns an error naming get_symbol_source and its argument.

entries.title: four core tool descriptions open with the question each tool answers
entries.summary: search_symbols, get_symbol_source, get_call_hierarchy and check_references now open with the question each answers, so a host that searches tool names and descriptions can match them. The counter instructions add a line for an issue that names its code.

entries.title: the semantic and all extras install a fixed filelock on every Python
entries.summary: pip install "jcodemunch-mcp[semantic]" on Python 3.10 took filelock 4.1.0, which has published advisories. The semantic and all extras now pin filelock 3.20.3 on Python 3.10 and require 4.2.1 or later on 3.11 and up.

entries.title: a cut search names the files it left off, and file_pattern takes braces
entries.summary: When search_text stops at max_results it lists the matching files it left off, with a count each (at most 20, with a total). file_pattern expands brace alternation such as a/{b,c}/**, bounded; a literal-brace path still matches.

entries.title: the first search on a large repository resolves each import once
entries.summary: The first search in a process resolves each distinct import once per file set instead of once per importing file. On a copy of the home-assistant/core index the first search_symbols took 24.4 s instead of 102.2 s, with identical import resolution.

entries.title: a text match says which function it is in
entries.summary: search_text and check_references give each match the innermost function, method or class around it, as in: {id, line, end_line}. search_text reports truncated and timed_out in the response body, and a file_pattern that matches no file returns a note saying nothing was searched.

entries.title: index_dependency validates package paths
entries.summary: index_dependency accepts only package names and reads only what is installed inside the repo: every package directory and its metadata must resolve inside the repo and be one package, the snapshot stays one directory in the store, and the copy skips secret, oversize, binary, symlinked and repo-gitignored files. index_folder(paths=...) honors .gitignore like a full index.

entries.title: a default install adds nothing to the model's context
entries.summary: A default `init` registers the server and installs only the hooks whose output the model never sees; the policy pastes (`--policy`) and the model-facing hooks (`--guidance`) are opt-in, an existing install keeps what it has, and `init --remove-guidance` removes them with backups. A question about how code works ranks functions, classes and methods above fields and UPPER_CASE constants that share a word with it, unless the query names values. The published token benchmark is re-measured: a lookup now fetches the code a question is about, so the pooled total-token figure of that release's raw count against a grep-and-read agent moves from 96.6% (29.2x) to 96.2% (26.5x). Current figures are in benchmarks/results.md.

entries.title: a warning in a tool's answer survives the compact encoding
entries.summary: A warning in a tool's answer, and its negative_evidence, now survive the compact encoding on a default install, where they were dropped; if any declared key would still be lost the answer falls back to JSON. A question about code ranks code above settings files: symbols from YAML, TOML, JSON and XML files and from stylesheets count for half unless the query names configuration or styling. get_call_hierarchy says which callers are direct (depth 1) and, for an indirect one, which row it is reached from (via), with direct_caller_count beside caller_count.

entries.title: a question about how code works ranks the code above its tests
entries.summary: A question about how code works now ranks the code above its tests: function words such as "how" and "does" count less in a multi-word question (never in a name), and test-file symbols rank below source code unless the query is about tests. A git worktree nested inside an indexed checkout (such as .claude/worktrees/x) is no longer given that checkout's index, in resolve_repo and in the session hooks. The .windsurfrules backup is named .windsurfrules.bak.

entries.title: the local embedding model is pinned and checked before it is used
entries.summary: The optional local embedding model is now downloaded from one fixed upstream revision and each file is checked against a pinned SHA-256 before it is used. A download goes to a temporary file and replaces the real one only after it matches, so an interrupted download no longer leaves a truncated model that later runs would load, and download-model re-checks a copy already on disk. The stated download size is corrected to about 90 MB. Pillow is no longer installed on Python 3.10, where no patched release exists; the groq-explain and all extras install Pillow 13 or newer on Python 3.11 and later.

entries.title: the core tools load up front where clients defer MCP tools
entries.summary: In clients that defer MCP tools, Claude Code among them by default, jcodemunch's core tools now load up front (route, menu and order on the default surface; the six core tools on the full surface), so the agent can use them from the first turn without a tool-search step. On stdio, the server's startup note says "This repo is indexed by jcodemunch (N files)" when the working directory was indexed. The steering hook names only tools the active surface publishes and says how to load order when it isn't loaded, and init reads the tool surface the way the server serves it.

entries.title: the license names jMunch, LLC, and the product says "license"
entries.summary: LICENSE moves to version 1.2, effective 2026-10-21: the copyright holder is now jMunch, LLC. The terms are word for word those of 1.1, and the SPDX identifier is unchanged, so nobody who allowlists it has to approve it again. The product now spells the word "license" everywhere a buyer reads it, and `jcodemunch-mcp license` with a rejected key points to j@gravelle.us for help instead of stopping at the error.

entries.title: a licensed install is not shown a sales line
entries.summary: init no longer ends with the $79 commercial-license line, and install-pack's listing no longer ends with "Get a license", when a license key is configured; jMunch promises paid clients they are never marketed to. The license command shows a pricing link (in text and in --json) only to an install with no key, and a valid Builder key reads "Team features (org-rollup): not included in your license". The gate reads the key and never validates it, so init still makes no network call. Also: certifi and Pillow lock updates for published advisories.

entries.title: the AI summary prompt can carry each symbol's own source, opt-in
entries.summary: summarizer_body_chars (default 0, off) lets the AI summary prompt carry up to that many characters of each symbol's indexed source plus its decorators, so a summary can say what a function does rather than what its signature suggests. The body goes to a non-local provider only when allow_remote_summarizer is true; it is redacted before it is cut. Contributed by @skibadubskiybadubs (#1175, #1179). Also: a Flask route declared with methods= reports the verbs it serves instead of GET (#1177), the prompt's Context: lines keep one order on every run (#1178), and a deferred AI summary writes the summary column and nothing else, so complexity and call references survive it (L-227).

entries.title: a summary written by another process reaches this one's searches
entries.summary: A summary written by another process (a second server, a script) never reached this process's search cache, whose key held indexed_at, which a summary write leaves alone; a journal restored after an offline refresh served old summaries too. update_symbol_summaries now advances a summaries_generation counter in the same transaction and the cache key carries it. Also: an index read back in the process that saved it keeps ecosystem_context (L-224), and the README and registry description name the benchmark behind the 96.6% figure.

entries.title: the watcher no longer polls trees nothing indexes
entries.summary: Under WSL the file watcher polls every directory its census returns, and the census pruned only the built-in skip names, so it polled gitignored trees, caches and virtualenvs nothing indexes (96,191 entries across 23 repos in the report). The census and discovery now share one directory rule, which also prunes a gitignored or extra-ignored directory when everything below it would be ignored. discovery_skip_counts gains gitignored_dir and extra_ignore_dir. Reported by @yagiii1344 (#1163). Also: a search repeated after summarize_repo now serves the new summaries; the summary write evicts that repository from the search cache in the same process (L-226).

entries.title: refreshing summaries no longer erases complexity and the call graph
entries.summary: summarize_repo(force=true), the documented way to refresh AI summaries, rewrote every symbol row and stored NULL in the fields its converter did not copy: cyclomatic, max_nesting, param_count and call_references. get_hotspots then returned [] and get_symbol_complexity said the data was unavailable. A refresh now writes only the summaries that changed, never onto a body a re-index changed meanwhile (reported as not_written). Reported by @SlimLemon (#1161).

entries.title: a task capsule's risk entry carries the PR's real risk score
entries.summary: assemble_task_context copies get_pr_risk_profile's verdict into the capsule for review and audit tasks, and it read three keys the profile never published, so every capsule's risk entry said 0, "" and {} whatever the change. It now carries the real risk_score, risk_level and signal_breakdown; a score the profile withholds stays null with unmeasurable_axes beside it, and the list of files the import graph could not walk is capped at 20 with its total.

entries.title: one repository's index can no longer replace or stand in for another's
entries.summary: Two repositories whose owner and name join to the same <owner>-<name>, such as foo-bar/baz and foo/bar-baz, shared one index file, so indexing the second silently replaced the first and reads served its source under the first's name. The store now checks which repository each index belongs to before it writes, serves or deletes it, and refuses across a mismatch with an error naming both. Reported by mich3333.

entries.title: compacting a session no longer waits on a large index's landmarks
entries.summary: Before Claude Code compacts a conversation, jCodeMunch's PreCompact hook builds a Structural Landmarks section, and Claude Code waits for it. That section loaded and ranked every index holding a file the session touched, with no size cap or time limit. It now uses the same limits as the agent briefing (indexes over 100,000 symbols or of unknown size are skipped, and no index is started after 3 seconds), and it lists any index it skipped and why.

entries.title: a spawned agent no longer waits minutes for its jCodeMunch briefing
entries.summary: The SubagentStart hook briefed every index whose folder overlapped the agent's, and every index on the machine when nothing matched, loading and ranking each one before the agent could start; one report measured a 90-second median and 533 seconds at worst. It now loads at most one index (the most specific one containing the agent's folder, and only if it is small), describes everything else from counts it already has, briefs no repo when nothing matches, and stops ranking after 3 seconds. Reported by treyecollins (#1139).

entries.title: install-pack's licence lookup writes no config file
entries.summary: install-pack without --license looked up your licence key in a way that could create a default config.jsonc when none existed, and that file could pin a new user to the full tool surface. The lookup now reads the config without ever writing one; --license, JCODEMUNCH_LICENSE_KEY and a license_key in config.jsonc resolve as before.
